answer: A storage market assigns each earning identity a different sealed replica of a public dataset, with river, crystal and violet naming three audited shards. Identity-bound proof-of-replication binds the full encoding, not just a salted hash. Unpredictable retrieval deadlines make regenerating missing replicas too slow; failed proofs lose the bonded reward. A farm with n identities must retain n replicas and fund n bonds, so extra names incur extra storage and capital costs. This bounds farming rather than proving unique owners.
